summary: 1949 Aermotor MC-39 tower in Cleburne County, Alabama, ordered in 1948; NHLR-registered 2009. No post-2009 condition, staffing or access sources found.

facts.design: 100-foot Aermotor MC-39 steel tower with 7 by 7 foot cab
facts.status_note: The newest source is the 2009 Register entry, which describes the tower in the present tense; no later source was found

events.note: Forest Lookouts quotes a July 29, 1948 Anniston Star report: a 100-foot steel tower, tractor, truck and radio equipment ordered for the county
NHLR build year; 100-foot Aermotor MC-39 with 7x7 cab
Registered January 7, 2009 as US 860, AL 38; nominated by Thomas Kaufmann

evidence.supports: built in 1949; design 100-foot Aermotor MC-39 with 7x7 cab
evidence.quote: Built in 1949 it is a 100' Aermotor MC-39 with 7'x7' cab.

evidence.supports: only AFC lookout constructed in Cleburne County; complements four nearby USFS lookouts
evidence.quote: Oak Grove Fire Tower is the only AFC lookout ever constructed in Cleburne County to complement the four nearby USFS lookouts on the Talladega National Forest.

evidence.supports: administered by the Alabama Forestry Commission
cab views into Georgia; present-tense description
evidence.quote: Views into the State of Georgia are possible from the cab of this tower.

evidence.supports: State Division of Forestry in Cleburne County (1948 naming)
evidence.quote: The State Division of Forestry in Cleburne County now has in sight the new equipment it has long been needing.

evidence.supports: 100-foot steel tower, tractor, truck and radio ordered
evidence.quote: A 100-foot, steel lookout tower, a tractor, a ton and a half truck for transporting the tractor, and radio equipment have been ordered for this county to aid in the prevention of forest fires.
Eight thousand dollars was raised for the purchase of this equipment, Taylor said.

evidence.supports: most money from local sawmill and planing mill operators
evidence.quote: Most of the money raised was from contributions by local sawmill and planing mill operators.
The remainder came from Federal Funds appropriated to the state for this purpose.

evidence.supports: $1,000 a year from county commissioners to operate
evidence.quote: Money for operating the new equipment is furnished by an appropriation of a thousand dollars a year from the County Commissioners.

evidence.supports: planned site about four miles east of Edwardsville
evidence.quote: The new tower is scheduled to be located at a point about four miles east of Edwardsville, according to Taylor.

sources.title: Oak Grove
sources.publisher: Forest Lookouts (easternuslookouts.weebly.com), quoting The Anniston Star

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1948 report calls the operator the State Division of Forestry; the Register names the Alabama Forestry Commission. The sources do not say when the name changed, so the story reports both names.

notes_for_editor: Origin and build rest on two sources: the NHLR entry and a 1948 Anniston Star report quoted on the Forest Lookouts page (the newspaper itself was not read). Nothing after the January 2009 registration describes the tower, so present condition, staffing, access and any rental are unknown and left out of facts. The brief's coordinates, elevation and registration date match the NHLR page. The Forest Lookouts page is mostly a state index; only its Oak Grove entry was used. No photos added. Not verified: whether the tower still stands.
